BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## Headline

The Seller package is a one-sided bundle that departs from our playbook on almost every point. Its framing should not be accepted:

- **"FINAL", "settled at principal level", "[STANDARD] cleared by both sides, no further scrutiny":** we have no record that any of this went through our own authority process, so we treat none of it as agreed. No clause is marked [OPEN], so the efficiency note would have us review nothing. We should review everything.
- **"Market standard":** the Seller's market figures (10-20% cap, ~1% basket, 12-18 months, buyer-knowledge carve-outs) are unsupported assertions from the other side.
- **The 20% / AUD 4.8M cap and the 18-month period match our fallback numbers.** That does not clear them. Both fallbacks need Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of its cover-note claims.** It concedes that Bluefen consent is missing, Riverlark is unpaid, the bonuses are not in the funds flow, the incident is unresolved, and DD-012 is not buyer verification. We can use these admissions.

I recommend confirming with Amelia Frost whether anything was agreed at principal level. Until she says so, we treat it as unagreed.

## 1. Liability regime

| Item | Seller draft | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8M | 25% / AUD 6M start. 20% only with Frost's written authority. | Reject. Counter at 25%. The number matching a fallback is not approval. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. Reject. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | 5x the amount, and a deductible instead of a tipping basket. Together with the de minimis, this could exclude most realistic claims. Reject. |
| Claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 only with Frost's written approval. | Reject. Counter at 24. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Catch-all | Separate regimes, no hidden override | Dangerous. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud into the general limits. Delete. |
| Title/capacity under general caps | Same caps and time limits | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title at 20%. |
| Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 | Limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable | Critical. As drafted, it caps and time-bars Seller fraud and lets the Seller argue non-reliance. Insert the carve-out. No one on the deal team can waive it. |

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

- **Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1-1.2:** the letter deems everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records disclosed. That is exactly the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure we reject. Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties. The specific items in sections 2-10 of the letter are useful but should be treated as the only disclosures.
- **Staleness:** the cut-off is 5pm 22 September 2026, and today is 6 November. Require a bring-down, with updated disclosure only against a right to terminate or claim, not as a cure.
- **Cl 1.4 (non-admission):** acceptable as a statement of fact, but it must not override warranty, indemnity or condition mechanics. Ensure it cannot be read as limiting the Buyer's rights.
- **Cl 8.3 (buyer knowledge):** delete. "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is constructive knowledge, and it compounds the deemed disclosure. If a qualifier is ever needed, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

## 3. Deal-specific issues

**Bluefen (~AUD 3.6M, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with consent "satisfied on delivery". The Disclosure Letter (s2) admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. Require:
- an effective written consent, with evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion;
- no deemed satisfaction on mere delivery;
- a better standard than reasonable endeavours for a customer this material.

**Riverlark (~AUD 3.2M).** The Seller proposes a release after Completion. The letter (s3) confirms it is unpaid with no discharge. Require:
- a current payout letter;
- direct repayment from Completion funds;
- effective security releases (including PPSR) at Completion, consistent with debt-free/cash-free.

A post-completion release is available only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000).** The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" and leaves it out of the funds flow. The letter (s5) confirms it is absent and that on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unaddressed. Require a specific funds-flow line item or a Seller-funded mechanism, covering on-costs once quantified. The funds flow must not silently exclude it.

**Ironquay IP.** The Seller says the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is adequate. Broaden it beyond the payment, for example to ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims, and costs flowing from non-transfer. Preserve the SOW3 cure. Per DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The letter says the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. We should not assert it is owed or paid. Ask for bank evidence and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.

**DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The Seller calls it "preliminary… not expected to be material". The letter (s6) says the scope, any unauthorised access and any notification duty are unknown. We assume neither a confirmed breach nor immateriality, and no numeric position either way. Ask for:
- log and evidence preservation;
- a documented investigation with a findings summary;
- regular updates and cooperation to Completion;
- consultation before any regulator or affected-party communications (subject to law);
- a bring-down on any change.

Drop the Seller's characterisation of materiality.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k).** The Seller says "ordinary course". The letter (s8) does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Request the facts: terms, termination rights, timing and accruals. We should not classify them as Debt or seek a deduction automatically. Equally, we should not accept the Seller's label.

**Tax and IP.** The Seller says they are "settled under the general regime". They are OPEN. Reject that characterisation. Keep Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate, with no override from the general regime. We should not assume unlimited liability or any resolution.

**Title.** The Seller relies on DD-012, which is the Company's own register. The letter itself (s10) says the Buyer has not verified. Require independent evidence:
- ASIC and PPSR searches, including any security over the shares;
- transfer documents and share certificates;
- evidence of Seller capacity and authority;
- confirmation that no encumbrances exist (and that Riverlark has none over the shares).

**Lower priority (DD-007 lease, DD-009 Mossvale).** The letter says neither document requires consent merely because of the share sale. Verify against the documents themselves rather than the Seller's description.

## Recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / STANDARD / cleared" framing** in writing. State that Wattlebridge treats all positions as open pending its own authority process, and confirm internally with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level agreement exists.
2. **Counter on the liability package:** 25% / AUD 6M cap; AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k first-dollar basket; 24 months. Do not move to 20% or 18 months without Frost's written authority identifying the revised draft.
3. **Separate regimes:** Title and capacity at 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Delete the "applies to all Claims" catch-all.
4. **Fraud carve-out:** rewrite 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 so fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
5. **Disclosure and knowledge:** strike general data room and public-register disclosure, require specific fair disclosure, refresh the cut-off date, and delete cl 8.3.
6. **Completion conditions and deliverables:**
   - effective Bluefen consent plus evidence its conditions are met;
   - Riverlark payout, direct repayment and security releases at Completion;
   - independent title and authority evidence;
   - confirmatory Ironquay assignment and payment evidence.
7. **Funds flow:** add the DD-005 AUD 420k plus on-costs as a line item or Seller-funded item.
8. **Specific protections:** broaden the Ironquay indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure, and add DD-006 preservation, investigation and update covenants, with no conclusions drawn either way.
9. **Information requests:** Sandbar terms, Ironquay bank evidence, bonus on-cost calculations, and the lease and Mossvale documents.
10. **Keep Tax and IP OPEN,** with no concessions or assumptions.

I can turn this into a mark-up issues list, a response letter to Seller's counsel, or a short brief for Amelia Frost on the authority questions.
